question: Built on four fused hydrocarbon rings instead of the long straight chains of a fat, a _____ is the odd shape among the lipids and the one hormones are cut from.
questions: Being a lipid, one of these crosses the membrane rather than stopping at it, so a _____ is met by a receptor inside the cell that switches genes on directly.
Fungi build ergosterol where animals build cholesterol, and an antifungal azole exploits that gap in the pathway to this kind of _____ without harming its patient.
abstract:
A steroid is a lipid built on four fused hydrocarbon rings rather than on the long straight chains of a fat. Cholesterol is the familiar one, and its rings are strongly hydrophobic while the single hydroxyl group at one end is weakly hydrophilic, which makes the whole molecule amphipathic. It is also the precursor of the steroid hormones, a diverse set of chemical messengers that all carry those same four rings and differ in the functional groups attached to them. Making one begins with the steroidogenic acute regulatory protein, which moves cholesterol to the inner mitochondrial membrane, where the enzyme CYP11A1 converts it to pregnenolone. The rest follows from there, pregnenolone giving progesterone and the corticosteroids while dehydroepiandrosterone gives the androgens and oestrogens.

Because a steroid is a lipid it crosses a membrane rather than stopping at it, and its receptor waits inside the cell and works as a ligand-activated transcription factor, so the hormone reaches the genes directly. Vitamin D belongs to the family as well, a secosteroid made in skin from 7-dehydrocholesterol, an intermediate of cholesterol synthesis, under ultraviolet B light, and acting through a receptor of exactly that kind. Plants build their own, and the brassinosteroids, the sixth class of plant hormone to be identified, govern growth and environmental adaptation in rice and are now a target for breeding. Fungi build ergosterol where animals build cholesterol, which is why irradiating a mushroom yields vitamin D2 rather than D3. That same gap is what the azole antifungals exploit, blocking lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase in the ergosterol pathway, and point mutations in the gene for it now turn up in Aspergillus fumigatus worldwide.
